The earlier 160 ns (dispatch.b300.r4, tail mode) is the fast class only. Superseded as a single constant by the two class values of dispatch_refill.b300.r4.

dispatch_refill.b300.r2.description: dispatch_refill run 2 (addendum 2): replay of the per-slot rule with 216 ns and the untruncated 0.513613 ns serial constant on four new cells (holds 2200 / 4500 / 9000, jitter 150, 6 waves) gives span within 0.9 %; steady gap 408-430 cycles measured against 438. The mean-gap criterion fails three of the four cells in generation 2 (measured 563-849 cycles against 1002-1672): the engine enters the first wave at cycle 0, the hardware spreads it over 1040-1250 cycles per SM.

dispatch_refill.b300.r4.description: dispatch_refill run 4 (protocol.json addendum 5). Refill gap per SM class over the six spin cells of runs 1, 2, 4 (three cards): fast 159.4 ns (154.0-170.9), slow 250.9 ns (245.1-262.3); the slow class is four whole topology gpcs, {2,5,6,7} on two of the three cards and {1,2,6,7} on the third -- the mask is the majority set, a declared choice. PREEXIT (griddepcontrol.launch_dependents): a CTA in which it was executed occupies the GPU-wide dispatch serializer for 1.00 x serial_ns_per_cta more; per CTA not per warp (1 / 2 / 4 of 4 warps: same span), linear in the fraction of CTAs (0-1000 permille), independent of where in the CTA it executes and of the launch attribute; replay within 2 % on 17 of 18 cells. Counter-example: 512-thread CTAs with PREEXIT, span 5 % above the replay (fast-class gap 313 -> about 480 cycles). Not modelled: first-wave spread; the slow class rising to about 685 cycles when every CTA does cold global reads at a hold of 3000 cycles or less.

Home-partition bimodal like the atomic round trip; median installed, no address axis.

fullgpu.mechtree.m3.global_atomic.rt.description: EXPERIMENTAL B300/SM103 dependent global atomic round trip (atom.global.add.u32, value feeds the next operand, one lane, one SM, unloaded; protocol global_atomic_protocol.json amendment 1, runs m3m4-r6a/r6b): over 64 distinct 128 B lines the cycles per link are BIMODAL by address -- 290-355 (near home L2 partition, ~50 % of lines) and 690-780 (far, ~50 %); plain loads over the same region stay single-mode (chase_l2 284-300 cycles), i.e. coherent ops travel to the line home partition. The leaf has no address axis, so the median over the 64 lines is installed: 503.0/500.7 cycles -> 247.1 ns (two cards 0.5 %). Both modes and shares are in the artifact (/per_run/*/atom_chain_addr).

l1_residency.b300.r2.description: B300 l1_residency protocol v4 (tools/microbench/crossings/l1_residency/protocol-v4.json; probe l1cap.cu v3: one CTA, lane-0 dependent ld.global.ca chase over F = 4..256 KiB in 4 KiB steps, random cyclic 128 B lines, warm then timed pass; --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs, SASS gate ok). The L1 data budget of a launch is set by the shared-memory configuration the driver selects (occupancy rule: smallest supported configuration >= n_res x (dynamic + static + 1 KiB), n_res = min(32 CTAs, 64 warps / block warps, 228 KiB / per-CTA need)), not by the launch's own shared bytes: the 10 default-hint cells (S 0 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 192 KiB x block 32 / 1024) give effective capacity E = 184 / 240 / 20 / 148 / 52 / 116 / 116 / 116 / 52 / 52 KiB with configurations 64 / 8 / 228 / 100 / 196 / 132 / 132 / 132 / 196 / 196 KiB (cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor equals n_res in every cell) and E + configuration = 248 KiB in all 10 cells of both runs (spread 0) -> data_array_bytes = 253952, reserved_bytes = 0 (measured; the 8 KiB below 256 KiB is the unusable part of the array, the same on both devices). The pinned-hint cells (v3 install path, unrealised) show that cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout does not pin the configuration (hint 0 / 4 / 8 / >= 15 % -> 8 / 100 / 164 / 228 KiB at S = 0; 44 % -> 228 at S = 0 but 132 at S = 64 KiB). Replaces the structural placeholder 262144 / 0 (placeholder.p0.memory.structure): the B300 budget is 248 KiB like the H100's, 8 KiB less than the placeholder. Engine finding handed to the engine line: l1_cap_lines should subtract the selected configuration, not the launch's shared bytes.

Replaces the placeholder 0 / 0 (blackwell.placeholder.mechanism_unmeasured); the m(D) curve is already 0.57 at D = 128 and 0 from D = 384 (h100: 0.85 at 128, ~0.1 from 384).

l2_merge.b300.r4.delivered.description: B300 l2_merge protocol v2 (same probe, set m1r4 with nsm(G) = floor(148/G) x G; sass gate PASS LDG.E.128 x8; image ncu; two runs x 5 trials). delivered_bytes_per_cycle = 14213.6 / 14201.1 (agree 0.09 %), both at ld_l2g_24mb_g002_lock (28.88 TB/s at 2032 MHz; r = 0.632, 37 % of the delivered bytes merged; +43 % over the disjoint reference 20.1 TB/s = 68.65 B/cycle/SM). Caveat recorded, not a derivation change: every lock and rot config on B300 delivers 100-104 B/cycle per SM regardless of G (h100: 58-103), so the maximum is bounded by the per-SM ingest rate of this 1024-thread LDG.E.128 streamer rather than by a visible GPU-wide merged-delivery knee; the installed value is therefore the largest SM-side aggregate this probe can show and may be a lower bound of the fabric ceiling. mechtree.w6.tmem.live_column_budget.description: B300/SM103 usable TMEM live-column allocation budget per SM: 512 columns, not physical SRAM size. tmem-capacity63: GPU-2e474239-050c-41f4-131c-029e7d60aa8b and GPU-ca19438d-f0cf-db63-9d37-d4ace0c4ac78; B300 SXM6 AC, CC10.3, driver 580.159.03, nvcc/cuobjdump 13.2.78, source cd0535954. Each GPU: 450 kernel observations, 44400 non-warmup same-SM CTA pairs across all 148 SMs, 2255093760 checked uint32 cells plus 22200 warmup pairs whose outcomes must agree. Five legal CG1 allocation sizes {32,64,128,256,512} independently crossed; two retention durations {65536,262144}; three launches, one warmup and two subsequent samples per launch. Concurrent 256+256 retains both full payloads; 512+32 waits for holder deallocation, with the extra wait following the retention-duration change. Bounds [512,544), at the ISA's 32-column allocation quantum, identify 512 usable columns. Both CTAs verify start/end SM identity and every cell in all 128 rows. Native allocation, permit relinquish, deallocation, STTM/LDTM and zero spills are SASS-checked. The field is an SM-shared budget, separate from the CTA address-space limit; native success/retry pressure remains unsupported without captured outcome facts. No allocation latency, issue interval, arbitration, fragmentation policy or CG2 timing is inferred from these capacity-only observations.

structural.v10.instruction_service.description: Engine audit (cpp/src/engine.cpp + job.cpp): Plan fields are installed via install_field (job.cpp:945-962) at leaf selection and committed through MechanismRuntime::commit only for fields the transition marks consumed. (a) backend_occupancy_cycles (field 8) is applied only when >0 (engine.cpp ~2941). (b) issue_group_resource_id (field 11) is applied only when != 0xFFFFFFFF (engine.cpp ~2955). (c) max_inflight/queue_class (fields 5/6) feed total_capacity_ready_cycle, but at (1,0) with backend_occupancy=0 the queued completion retires at the admission cycle so the cap can never bind -- verified empirically: fma group max_inflight 1->4 + queue_class 0->7 left CU-DSL-F16 cycles identical (17178). (d) For classes with a global memory access the memory model supplies result/completion and the plan fields are unconsumed (consumed_plan_fields |= 6 only when no access, engine.cpp ~1945; sentinel 1 still required where lifecycle-contract rows exist, job.cpp:1463-1466); observed application masks: LDG/STG commit only field 11, LDS leaves fields 1,7 unconsumed (dependency.result + shared-issue rows carry them), STS leaves field 7 unconsumed (storage.shared issue interval). NOTE: predicated_off leaves ARE consumed -- flipping xu predicated_off issue_interval 8->40 moved misc-thr launches 14-17 by ~5x; their commit transitions record mask 0, a telemetry blind spot, not dead fields.

structural.v10.ldgsts_service_start.description: Engine audit: the kind-21 interval is read at engine.cpp ~2220 but consumed only in reserve_background_resource on the !has_global_memory_access path (~2361/~2437, requiring lifecycle AsynchronousTransfer). Predicated-off LDGSTS has lifecycle predicated_noop (strict_timing.py lifecycle rule) so it never reaches the consumed path; active LDGSTS carries captured global sectors -> has_global_memory_access, and job_v10 now raises FormatError for an active LDGSTS without captured sectors (fail-closed). The field therefore never binds for any reachable class; value 1 is the sentinel.

structural.v10.lds_sts_cta_window.description: The remote_smem=1 children of storage.shared.{issue,acceptance_sm,visibility} are unreachable: on sm_103a LDS/STS address only the executing CTA's shared::cta window, and ld/st.shared::cluster to a peer CTA compile to generic LD.E/ST.E through the cluster shared window (S2R SR_SWINHI + PRMT; verified with nvcc 13.2.78 on a mapa + ld/st.shared::cluster kernel and on semantic-suite cl02_cluster_split_arrive_dsmem, artifacts/mechtree/dsm-test/). tracer_v5's RANK fact for an LDS/STS operand is getctarank of the own-window address (= issuer rank). strict_timing.py now rejects a captured remote_smem=1 on an LDS/STS root (FormatError), so these leaves never bind; values are kept as sentinels. Note: DSMEM LD/ST themselves are not routed to these rows (they are classified by memory_space), a converter scope question outside this tree.

structural.v10.predicated_noop.retiremen.description: V10 LifecycleContract PredicatedNoop (selector 7) requires result_latency=1 and completion_latency=1 in both mechanism installation and job validation. These are fixed plan-format retirement sentinels, not measured hardware dependency or completion latencies. The instruction produces no destination or asynchronous background work. Issue cadence, resource routing and all other predicated-off fields retain their independent evidence.

structural.v10.single_copy_admission_equ.description: Engine audit (cpp/src/engine.cpp): for an instruction.service plan with max_inflight 1 on a resource with copy_count 1 and max_inflight_per_copy 1 (every instruction resource in resources.json except storage_tma_tensor_per_sm), the primary reservation blocks the next admission on that copy until max(lifecycle_start + issue interval (reserve_resource), lifecycle_start + backend_occupancy_cycles (resource_completion_cycle, capacity_ready_cycle, engine.cpp ~L785-855 and ~L2045-2067)). A backend hold B and an issue interval are therefore observationally identical; the hardware cadence is carried by issue_interval_cycles under its own evidence, and (max_inflight 1, queue_class 0, B 0) is the canonical encoding - queue_class and max_inflight only cap reservations still incomplete at the candidate cycle, which never exist when B = 0. Not applicable to tensor/TMEM async ops (field 8 is the SM async-pipe hold, sm_async_service_occupancy_op) or TMA (max_inflight_per_copy 16). Predicated-off tensor occurrences carry no tensor dynamic (job_v10.py), so the rule covers their predicated_off parts too.

structural.v10.tmem_result_row.description: install_tmem_result sets result = lifecycle_start + mandatory storage.tmem.load/store row (engine.cpp ~L2484-2518; throws when the row is missing); completion = max(plan completion, result) and rows are >= 1, so the sentinel 1 never binds. STTM census wb=7. LDTM.STAT is TensorOp::TmemLoadStat and takes the same install_tmem_result path as LDTM (engine.cpp ~2495-2510: kind-13 row + kind-43 extra), so plan fields 1/2 never bind.
